title: Your Brain Is Not What You Think It Is, with Lisa Feldman Barrett, PhD

sentences.en: When you're angry or do something impulsive, that's your reptilian brain in action, right?
sentences.zh: 当你感到愤怒或做出一时冲动的行为时，那是你的爬行动物脑在起作用，对吗？

sentences.en: And if you talk yourself out of that impulsive act or gain control over your wrath, that's your neocortex at work, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 如果你说服自己克制那种冲动行为，或者控制住你的怒火，那是你的新皮层在发挥作用，不是吗？

sentences.en: And those emotions you feel, such as grief when a loved one dies, or joy at the birth of a child, those are just things that happen to you in reaction to events in your life,
sentences.zh: 而你所感受到的那些情绪，比如挚爱离世时的悲伤，或是孩子出生时的喜悦，这些只是你对生活中发生的事情做出反应时发生在你身上的事情，

sentences.en: correct?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And they're universal across cultures, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 而且它们在不同的文化中都是相通的，对吗？

sentences.en: Well, maybe not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许不见得。

sentences.en: What if emotions are things that our brain constructs to make sense of the signals it gets from our body and from the world around us?
sentences.zh: 如果情绪是我们的大脑为了理解它从我们身体以及周围世界接收到的信号而构建出来的东西呢？

sentences.en: What if the way you think about your brain and how and why it functions is just plain wrong?
sentences.zh: 如果你对大脑的看法，以及它是如何及为何运作的理解完全是错的呢？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学对话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Lisa Feldman Barrett, a distinguished professor of psychology at
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是丽莎·费尔德曼·巴雷特博士，她是东北大学的杰出心理学

sentences.en: Northeastern University.
sentences.zh: 教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Barrett has spent more than three decades studying emotion.
sentences.zh: 巴雷特博士从事情绪研究已有三十多年。

sentences.en: Her research has helped to develop the idea that the human brain creates emotions by predicting rather than reacting to what happens in the world around us.
sentences.zh: 她的研究有助于形成这样一种观点：人类的大脑不是对周围世界发生的事情做出反应，而是通过预测来创造情绪。

sentences.en: She's published more than 240 scientific papers and is also a prolific science communicator, writing articles and books about brain science for the general public.
sentences.zh: 她发表了240多篇科学论文，同时也是一位多产的科学传播者，为大众撰写了大量关于脑科学的文章和书籍。

sentences.en: Her two most recent books are How Emotions Are Made, published in 2017, and Seven and a Half
sentences.zh: 她最近的两本书是2017年出版的《情绪是如何构成的》（How Emotions Are Made）以及11月问世的《关于大脑的七个半

sentences.en: Lessons About the Brain, which came out in November.
sentences.zh: 堂课》（Seven and a Half Lessons About the Brain）。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Barrett.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天加入我们，巴雷特博士。

sentences.en: Oh, it's a pleasure to be here, Kim.
sentences.zh: 哦，很高兴能来到这里，金。

sentences.en: I want to start with an idea that opens your new book, which is that the main purpose of the brain is not to think, but to regulate our bodies.
sentences.zh: 我想从你新书开头的一个观点开始，那就是大脑的主要目的不是思考，而是调节我们的身体。

sentences.en: This may seem counterintuitive or come as a surprise to some of our listeners.
sentences.zh: 这可能看起来有些反直觉，或者会让我们的某些听众感到意外。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, can you explain how you came to this conclusion and why it's so important?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你能解释一下你是如何得出这个结论的，以及为什么它如此重要吗？

sentences.en: I actually started with the question of why do we even have a brain?
sentences.zh: 我其实是从“我们为什么会有大脑”这个问题开始着手的。

sentences.en: That blob of meat between your ears is the most expensive organ that you have in your whole body.
sentences.zh: 你两耳之间的那团肉是你全身最昂贵的器官。

sentences.en: And so why do we even have a brain?
sentences.zh: 那么我们为什么还要长个大脑呢？

sentences.en: And so what I did was I went back in the literature and I looked in the literature on evolutionary neuroscience to a time when animals on the earth didn't have brains and looked
sentences.zh: 所以我做的是，我查阅了演化神经科学的文献，回溯到地球上的动物还没有大脑的时期，研究了

sentences.en: at the evolution of the brain and found some really remarkable evidence that brains evolved under the selection pressure of predation.
sentences.zh: 大脑的演化，并发现了一些非常显著的证据，表明大脑是在捕食的选择压力下演化而来的。

sentences.en: So during the Cambrian period, animals learned to hunt one another deliberately and eat each other.
sentences.zh: 所以在寒武纪时期，动物学会了刻意互相猎杀并吃掉对方。

sentences.en: And it's not that animals didn't eat each other before then, but there was very little evidence of actual hunting.
sentences.zh: 并不是说在此之前动物不吃对方，但几乎没有什么证据表明存在实际的捕食行为。

sentences.en: And so under the pressure, selection pressure of hunting, what happened is that bodies got bigger and required much more coordination of internal bodily systeMs.
sentences.zh: 因此在捕食的选择压力下，发生的情况是身体变得更大，这需要对内部身体系统进行更多的协调。

sentences.en: Because animals without brains don't have very much going on inside.
sentences.zh: 因为没有大脑的动物内部并没有发生太多的事情。

sentences.en: They have some internal coordination, but not very much.
sentences.zh: 它们有一些内部协调，但非常有限。

sentences.en: And they really have no sophisticated senses to speak of.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上也没有什么复杂的感官可言。

sentences.en: That is, they don't see, they don't hear, they don't smell.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它们看不见，听不见，也闻不到。

sentences.en: They really don't know very much about the world outside their own bodies.
sentences.zh: 它们对自身身体之外的世界其实知之甚少。

sentences.en: And what you see under predation is that bodies get bigger, senses evolve, and brains appear.
sentences.zh: 而你在捕食现象下看到的是，身体变大了，感官演化出来了，大脑也出现了。

sentences.en: And if you look at the anatomy of the brain, what you see is that at the core of the brain,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看大脑的解剖结构，你会发现，在大脑的核心，

sentences.en: even at the core of the cortex, cerebral cortex, are the regions that are regulating the systems
sentences.zh: 甚至在大脑皮层（大脑皮层）的核心，都是那些调节你身体系统的区域，

sentences.en: of your body, your immune system, your metabolism and endocrine system, your autonomic nervous system, and your skeletal muscle system.
sentences.zh: 你的免疫系统、新陈代谢和内分泌系统、自主神经系统以及骨骼肌肉系统。

sentences.en: And the networks in the brain that are responsible for remembering and thinking and seeing even are actually involved in regulating the body.
sentences.zh: 大脑中负责记忆、思考甚至视觉的网络实际上也参与了身体的调节。

sentences.en: And so the bottom line is that we do think, and we do feel, and we do see, but we do those things in the service of regulating the systems of the body.
sentences.zh: 因此，归根结底，我们的确会思考、会感受、也会看，但我们做这些事情是为了服务于调节身体系统的功能。

sentences.en: Now, we don't experience every feeling of gratitude or sadness, every hug we give, every insult we bear as having anything to do with the body, but it does.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们并不觉得每一次感激或悲伤的感觉、每一次给出的拥抱、每一次忍受的侮辱都与身体有任何关系，但事实确实如此。

sentences.en: And the reason why this is important is that many of the things that we think of as mental, like depression, illnesses like depression and anxiety, or even just things like seeing
sentences.zh: 之所以这很重要，是因为许多我们认为是精神层面的事情，比如抑郁症等疾病，甚至仅仅是像视觉或

sentences.en: or thinking, actually have important aspects to them that are related to the body.
sentences.zh: 思考这样的事情，其实都有着与身体相关的重要方面。

sentences.en: So depression, for example, in addition to being a mental illness and having immune functioning problems is also a metabolic illness, actually.
sentences.zh: 比如抑郁症，除了是一种精神疾病并伴有免疫功能问题之外，实际上它也是一种代谢性疾病。

sentences.en: And that's why it's important that we understand it really starts to break down the boundary between the mental and the physical.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它很重要，因为它开始打破精神和身体之间的界限。

sentences.en: And so, you know, we can understand, for example, that all mental disorders actually have basic physical processes that are in disarray.
sentences.zh: 因此，你知道，我们可以理解，例如，所有精神失调实际上都有着处于紊乱状态的基本生理过程。

sentences.en: And also things we think of as mental, physical illnesses like cardiovascular disease and so on actually have mental aspects to them, which are really important to understand.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们认为是精神层面的事情，以及心血管疾病等生理疾病，实际上也都有着非常重要的精神层面，这是我们需要去理解的。

sentences.en: So a few moments ago, you talked about the brain being the most expensive organ.
sentences.zh: 所以刚才你谈到大脑是最昂贵的器官。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Metabolically speaking, your brain costs you 20% of your metabolic budget.
sentences.zh: 从代谢角度来说，你的大脑消耗了你20%的代谢预算。

sentences.en: That's more than your heart.
sentences.zh: 这比你的心脏还要多。

sentences.en: That's more than your lungs.
sentences.zh: 比你的肺还要多。

sentences.en: That's more than your liver.
sentences.zh: 比你的肝脏还要多。

sentences.en: It's a very expensive organ to keep running.
sentences.zh: 维持它的运转是一个非常昂贵的器官。

sentences.en: All those little neurons and so on, it's really expensive, actually, metabolically speaking.
sentences.zh: 所有那些小神经元等等，从代谢角度来说真的非常昂贵。

sentences.en: And it turns out that metabolic efficiency is a major selection pressure, not just on any species that's alive.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，代谢效率不仅对任何存活的物种是一个主要的选拔压力，

sentences.en: It's true that it also, you know, it's important for the evolution of any species.
sentences.zh: 而且对任何物种的演化来说，它也很重要，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's also important for your health, mental and physical.
sentences.zh: 它对你的身心健康同样至关重要。

sentences.en: If you have metabolic dysregulation or things are not running as efficiently metabolically, and I'm not just talking about circulating glucose or something, you know, that's like
sentences.zh: 如果你有代谢失调或者说代谢运行效率不高，我指的不仅仅是循环中的葡萄糖之类的东西，你知道的，那是

sentences.en: one very small part of a very large, complicated system.
sentences.zh: 庞大复杂系统中的一小部分。

sentences.en: If your energy regulation is not proceeding in a metabolically efficient way, you will get sick.
sentences.zh: 如果你的能量调节没有以代谢高效的方式进行，你就会生病。

sentences.en: And are our brains more expensive than other mammalian brains?
sentences.zh: 那么我们的大脑比其他哺乳动物的大脑消耗更多吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we have this big, big hunk of meat up there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在上面长了这么一大坨肉。

sentences.en: Yes, they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们确实如此。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Primates, let's say, relative to other mammals, primates do have bigger brains relative to their body size than other mammals do.
sentences.zh: 灵长类动物，比方说，与其他哺乳动物相比，灵长类动物的大脑相对于它们的体型确实比其他哺乳动物更大。

sentences.en: And humans have bigger brains.
sentences.zh: 而人类拥有更大的大脑。

sentences.en: But I would say that, you know, the size of the cerebral cortex is not any bigger than you would expect for a primate who has a brain of our size.
sentences.zh: 但我要说的是，你知道，大脑皮层的大小并不比你对一个拥有我们这样体型大脑的灵长类动物所预期的要大。

sentences.en: So it's not like our cerebral cortex is so big relative to the rest of our brain.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说我们的大脑皮层相对于我们大脑的其余部分来说那么大。

sentences.en: It's just we have a big brain relative to our body size, and our cerebral cortex is as big as you might expect for a creature who has, you know, a brain of our size.
sentences.zh: 只是相对于我们的体型来说我们有一个很大的大脑，而我们的大脑皮层对于一个拥有我们这样体型大脑的生物来说，正如你所预期的那样大。

sentences.en: But there is some genetic upregulation in the human brain that makes it more expensive to run, particularly in the cerebral cortex, in particular layers of the cerebral cortex that
sentences.zh: 但在人类大脑中确实存在一些基因上调，使其运转成本更高，特别是在大脑皮层中，在与我们能力相关的大脑皮层特定层中，

sentences.en: have to do with our ability to, so I guess you could say, compress information, summarize information from multiple sources so that we can do things like abstraction.
sentences.zh: 所以我想你可以说，是为了压缩信息，从多个来源总结信息，以便我们能够做诸如抽象之类的事情。

sentences.en: Another what might be a surprising point to some people in your book, I think I alluded
sentences.zh: 在你的书中，对某些人来说可能是一个令人惊讶的观点，我想我在引言中

sentences.en: to it a little bit in the introduction, is the way that many of us were taught about the brain is wrong.
sentences.zh: 稍微提到了一点，那就是我们许多人被灌输的关于大脑的知识是错误的。

sentences.en: So a lot of our listeners, I'm sure, remember learning that there are three parts of the human brain.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的很多听众，我确信，都记得学过人类大脑有三个部分。

sentences.en: You've been asked this a million times.
sentences.zh: 这个问题你已经被问过一百万次了。

sentences.en: We think there's the lizard or reptilian brain that controls our basic bodily functions.
sentences.zh: 我们认为有控制我们基本身体功能的蜥蜴脑或爬行动物脑。

sentences.en: There's the emotional brain.
sentences.zh: 还有情绪脑。

sentences.en: And then there's the rational brain, the neocortex that's like the pinnacle of evolution and makes us supposedly superior to other animals.
sentences.zh: 然后是理性脑，即新皮层，它就像是演化的巅峰，据称使我们比其他动物更具优越性。

sentences.en: But you say this is incorrect.
sentences.zh: 但你说这是不正确的。

sentences.en: So where did the idea of a triune brain come from?
sentences.zh: 那么三位一体大脑的概念是从哪里来的呢？

sentences.en: And how do we know that it's wrong?
sentences.zh: 我们又是怎么知道它是错的呢？

sentences.en: Okay, so I gotta say, I'm happy to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我得说，我很高兴谈论这个。

sentences.en: I have been asked about this a lot, but I'm so happy to talk about it because it's like one of the most pervasive myths, modern myths in science.
sentences.zh: 这个问题我被问过很多次，但我非常高兴谈论它，因为它是科学中最普遍的神话之一，现代神话之一。

sentences.en: It's not even wrong, is what I would say, Kim.
sentences.zh: 金，我想说这甚至不能算错。

sentences.en: And I also have to say that this is not my research, right?
sentences.zh: 我也必须说明，这不是我的研究，对吧？

sentences.en: Like this is, I don't do research on this topic, although I do research on brain organization and its relevance for psychological functioning.
sentences.zh: 就像这个，我不做这个主题的研究，尽管我研究大脑组织及其与心理功能的相关性。

sentences.en: And I do research on the structure and function of tissue that is called limbic, but it's not called limbic because it's about emotion.
sentences.zh: 我也研究被称为边缘系统的组织的结构和功能，但它被称为边缘系统并不是因为它与情绪有关。

sentences.en: It's really more about the anatomical structure of the tissue.
sentences.zh: 它其实更多的是关于组织的解剖结构。

sentences.en: But let me just say that the idea of a triune brain, a brain in three layers, really can be,
sentences.zh: 但请容许我直言，三位一体大脑的概念，即三层大脑，实际上可以追溯到，

sentences.en: I've traced it all the way back to Plato.
sentences.zh: 我一直把它追溯到了柏拉图那里。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Because, you know, Plato talked about the soul or the psyche, which is not exactly the same as a mind, but for present purposes, it's like close enough.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，柏拉图谈到了灵魂或心灵（psyche），这不完全等同于思维，但就目前的目的而言，这就足够接近了。

sentences.en: He talked about the psyche as having, the human psyche is having three parts, one part for instinct, one part for emotion, which he represented as two beasts, right?
sentences.zh: 他谈到心灵有，人类的心灵有三个部分，一部分用于本能，一部分用于情绪，他将其表现为两只野兽，对吧？

sentences.en: Two horses.
sentences.zh: 两匹马。

sentences.en: And then a charioteer, which is human rationality, which obviously controls the beaSt.
sentences.zh: 然后是一个御者，也就是人类的理性，它显然控制着那头野兽。

sentences.en: And so right there, you have this idea of an inner beast and a rational part.
sentences.zh: 所以就在那里，你有了一个内心野兽和理性部分的概念。

sentences.en: And they're in constant battle for control of the chariot, of your behavior.
sentences.zh: 它们在不断争夺对战车、对你行为的控制权。

sentences.en: That's basically the idea.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是这个想法。

sentences.en: And so, you know, fast forward like a couple of thousand years and, you know, we're in the era of modern neuroscience, like in the, you know, mid 20th century.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，快进几千年，然后，你知道，我们处于现代神经科学的时代，比如在，你知道，20世纪中期。

sentences.en: And you have scientists who are using the best tools available to them, which is, you know, the naked eye, or maybe some not so powerful microscopes with some dyes.
sentences.zh: 然后你会发现科学家们使用的是他们手头最好的工具，也就是，你知道，肉眼，或者可能是一些带有某些染料的不那么强大的显微镜。

sentences.en: And, you know, you look at a lizard brain and lizard brain looks like it has a set of parts.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，你看一个蜥蜴的大脑，蜥蜴的大脑看起来像是由一组部件组成的。

sentences.en: And then you look at a early mat, like a small mammal brain, like a, like a rat.
sentences.zh: 然后你看一个早期的哺乳动物，比如一个小哺乳动物的大脑，比如，比如一只老鼠。

sentences.en: And you all look there, look like there are some extra parts there.
sentences.zh: 然后你看那里，看起来那里有一些额外的部件。

sentences.en: And then you, you know, look at a human, you're like, oh, wow, there's really, definitely a really big extra part there.
sentences.zh: 然后你，你知道，看一个人类，你会觉得，哦，哇，那里真的绝对有一个非常大的额外部件。

sentences.en: And so the idea that really grew out of this, that comes from Paul McLean, who was a neuroscientist
sentences.zh: 所以真正从中滋生出来的这个想法，来自于保罗·麦克林（Paul MacLean），他曾是一名神经科学家，

sentences.en: in Boston, actually, where, where I live in the 1940s, is this idea that lizards have circuitry for instincts.
sentences.zh: 实际上就在波士顿，也就是我居住的地方，在20世纪40年代，这个观点认为蜥蜴拥有用于本能在内的神经回路。

sentences.en: And then layered on top of that evolved the limbic system, limbic meaning border, which is
sentences.zh: 然后在它之上演化出了边缘系统，边缘（limbic）意思是边界，这

sentences.en: really old cortex, considered to be old cortex, um, that borders these, um, you know, lizard parts, um, which is where emotions live.
sentences.zh: 被认为是古皮层，被认为是一个古老的皮层，嗯，它环绕着这些，嗯，你知道的，蜥蜴的部件，嗯，这也是情绪居住的地方。

sentences.en: And then layered on top of that is the new part of the cortex, the neocortex, which is where rationality lives, the pinnacle, as you say, of evolution.
sentences.zh: 然后叠加上去的是皮层的新部分，即新皮层，这是理性居住的地方，正如你所说，是演化的巅峰。

sentences.en: Um, and so there are a couple of things wrong with this view.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这种观点有几个错误之处。

sentences.en: One is that, um, evolution, we aren't the pinnacle of anything.
sentences.zh: 一个是，嗯，演化，我们并不是任何东西的巅峰。

sentences.en: Evolution didn't aim itself at us, um, to use a paraphrase wording, um, uh, from, um, Henry
sentences.zh: 演化并不是以我们为目标的，嗯，借用古生物学家亨利·盖伊（Henri Guy）的一句化石措辞，

sentences.en: Guy, the paleontologist, Henry Guy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，来自，嗯，亨利·盖伊。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, animals are well adapted to their niche.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，动物非常适应它们的生态位。

sentences.en: If they still, if a species still is around, you know, after a couple of, um, hundred thousand years then, um, or, or longer, then it means it's well adapted to its niche.
sentences.zh: 如果它们仍然，如果一个物种在经历了几十万年之后，嗯，或者，或者更长时间，仍然存在，嗯，那就意味着它非常适应它的生态位。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, other animals have some pretty miraculous abilities to do things that we don't have, frankly, and that we endow our superheroes with.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，其他动物拥有一些相当神奇的能力，可以做我们所没有的事情，坦白说，那是我们赋予超级英雄的能力。

sentences.en: So yes, it's true.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，这确实是真的。

sentences.en: We can do some pretty amazing things as humans, but other animals can do very amazing things like grow back limbs.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们可以做一些相当了不起的事情，但其他动物也能做非常了不起的事情，比如肢体再生。

sentences.en: Yeah, we can't fly.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们不会飞。

sentences.en: We can't grow back limbs.
sentences.zh: 我们无法肢体再生。

sentences.en: We, we definitely can't, um, grow new neurons in most of our brains, whereas other animals, there are animals who can do all of those things or each of those things.
sentences.zh: 我们，我们绝对无法，嗯，在我们大脑的大部分区域长出新的神经元，而其他动物，有些动物可以做所有这些事情或者其中的每一件事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But more importantly, the evidence for molecular genetics, when you peer in deep into the cells,
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，来自分子遗传学的证据，当你深入观察细胞内部时，

sentences.en: um, the, the molecular structure of cells, and you look at the genes, uh, deep within what you see really clear evidence that brains did not evolve like sedimentary rock, you
sentences.zh: 嗯，细胞的分子结构，当你观察基因时，嗯，在深处，你所看到的是非常清晰的证据，表明大脑的演化并不像沉积岩那样，

sentences.en: know, or what I, the way I think of it is, you know, you've got this like deep animal beast, like inner ancient beaSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，或者说我的看法是，你知道，你拥有这种深层的动物野兽般的内在古代野兽。

sentences.en: And then late, you know, what evolved on top of that was, you know, rationality, like, like, uh, icing on an already baked cake, you know, brains didn't evolve that way.
sentences.zh: 然后晚期，你知道，在它之上演化出来的是，嗯，理性，就像，就像，已经烤好的蛋糕上的糖霜一样，你知道，大脑并不是那样演化的。

sentences.en: They just didn't.
sentences.zh: 它们根本就不是那样。

sentences.en: That's the evidence.
sentences.zh: 这就是证据。

sentences.en: And the evidence has been around for more than 50 years and yet, um, hasn't managed to percolate its way into not just into the public sphere, but into psychology textbooks.
sentences.zh: 这个证据已经存在了50多年，然而，嗯，它却没能渗透进公众领域，甚至没能进入心理学教科书。

sentences.en: Like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 就像是，是的。

sentences.en: Anytime you read that the amygdala and other parts of the limbic system, which I would put in scare quotes, because there is no limbic system in your brain, um, anytime, uh, you
sentences.zh: 每当你读到杏仁核和边缘系统的其他部分（我会给它加上引号，因为你大脑中并没有边缘系统），嗯，每当你，

sentences.en: know, you read that the amygdala or the limbic system is being regulated by the prefrontal cortex, that is a phrasing, which rests on this old, really mistaken idea, um, that, you
sentences.zh: 你知道，读到杏仁核或边缘系统正受到前额叶皮层的调节时，这种表述，是建立在这样一个古老且非常错误的观点之上的，即，

sentences.en: know, you have this inner beast lurking inside your brain, which is constantly in battle with your more sensible, rational self.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你的大脑深处潜伏着一头内在的野兽，它一直在与你更明智、理性的自我进行战斗。

sentences.en: And that the outcome of your, you know, that you're, when your rational side wins, you're healthy and moral.
sentences.zh: 并且你的，你知道的，结果是，当你的理性一面获胜时，你是健康且有道德的。

sentences.en: And when your, uh, inner beast wins, you're either, uh, you know, if your inner beast wins because, um, you didn't try hard enough, then you're not moral.
sentences.zh: 而当你的，嗯，内在野兽获胜时，你要么，嗯，你知道，如果你的内在野兽获胜是因为，嗯，你没有足够努力，那么你就是不道德的。

sentences.en: And, uh, if your inner beast wins because you, um, you know, there's something wrong, then you're sick.
sentences.zh: 并且，嗯，如果你的内在野兽获胜是因为你，嗯，你知道，有什么地方不对劲，那么你就是生病了。

sentences.en: That's just a, that's just a, it's a morality tale, um, but it doesn't reflect actually the biology of how we got these miraculous brains to begin with.
sentences.zh: 那只是一个，那只是一个，这是一个道德故事，嗯，但它并没有实际反映我们最初如何拥有这些神奇大脑的生物学原理。

sentences.en: You, you make another really interesting point in, in your new book that I think is something, another myth busting point.
sentences.zh: 你在你的新书里还提出了另一个非常有趣的观点，我认为这也是一个打破神话的观点。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people have the sense that parts of our brains kind of go dormant from time to time and we're not using them.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都觉得我们大脑的某些部分不时会进入休眠状态，而我们并没有在使用它们。

sentences.en: And I think what you're saying is neurons are firing all the time.
sentences.zh: 我想你要表达的是神经元一直在放电。

sentences.en: Maybe you can explain a little bit about how, how that works and why.
sentences.zh: 也许你可以稍微解释一下它是如何运作的以及为什么会这样。

sentences.en: So if you look back in the history of, of how neurons were, were discovered and how they
sentences.zh: 所以如果你回溯神经元是如何被发现以及它们是如何被研究的历史，比如在20世纪50年代，研究神经元属性的一种方法是取一个巨大的乌贼神经元，

sentences.en: were studied, like in the 1950s, for example, one way to study the properties of a neuron was to take a big squid neuron,
sentences.zh: 字面意思就是把它从大脑中取出来并铺在

sentences.en: like literally take it out of the brain and lay it out on
sentences.zh: 桌子上。

sentences.en: a table.
sentences.zh: 当你把一个你能看得到的单神经元铺在桌子上时，因为这些就像巨大的乌贼一样拥有，你知道的，它们拥有一个你可以用

sentences.en: And when you lay out a single neuron on a table that you can see, cause these are like really giant squids have like very, you know, they have a neuron that you can see with the
sentences.zh: 肉眼看到的神经元。

sentences.en: naked eye.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，它是休眠的。

sentences.en: As I understand it, it's dormant.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，它是休眠的。

sentences.en: And then you have to stimulate it with electricity to get it to produce an action potential down its axon.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须用电流刺激它，让它沿轴突产生动作电位。

sentences.en: And this is very conveniently consistent with the idea that the stimulus response idea that has really been around in psychology, really since the inception of psychology, right?
sentences.zh: 这与心理学中一直存在的刺激-反应观点非常吻合，可以说是自心理学诞生以来就存在，对吧？

sentences.en: So psychology, um, as a field was, was a field of full mental philosophy until the mid 19th
sentences.zh: 所以心理学，嗯，作为一个领域，在19世纪中期之前一直是充满精神哲学的领域

sentences.en: century when philosophers and, uh, neuro and neurologists and physiologists started to use
sentences.zh: 直到哲学家、神经学家和生理学家开始利用

sentences.en: the methods available to them from the physiology lab and from, from, um, patients with lesions
sentences.zh: 生理实验室以及病变患者身上获得的可用方法

sentences.en: to try to search for the physical basis of the psychological categories, um, that, that were in mental philosophy.
sentences.zh: 试图去寻找精神哲学中那些心理学范畴的物理基础。

sentences.en: So the physical basis of memory, the physical basis of emotion, the physical basis of perception and so on.
sentences.zh: 也就是记忆的物理基础、情绪的物理基础、感知的物理基础等等。

sentences.en: And the idea was that, you know, the brain is stimulated.
sentences.zh: 当时的观点是，你看，大脑受到了刺激。

sentences.en: The mind is stimulated by something in the world.
sentences.zh: 心灵受到世界上某事物的刺激。

sentences.en: And then maybe some processing goes on inside and then there's a response.
sentences.zh: 然后大脑内部可能会进行一些处理，接着就会产生反应。

sentences.en: So it's stimulus response jazzed up.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是加了点料的刺激-反应论。

sentences.en: This was very consistent with, you know, what happens when you look at an individual neuron lying on a table, it's dormant and you have to stimulate.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合当你看着放在桌上的单个神经元时发生的情况：它处于休眠状态，你必须去刺激它。

sentences.en: In order for it to fire, but that is not how neurons work when they are actually in situ with other neurons, bathed in chemicals, uh, and, and, uh, you know, oxygen and so on.
sentences.zh: 为了让它放电，但这不是神经元在实际与其他神经元共存时的运作方式，当时它们沐浴在化学物质、氧气等环境中。

sentences.en: Neurons are constantly talking to each other.
sentences.zh: 神经元在不断地彼此交流。

sentences.en: Your brain is basically having a conversation with itself throughout your entire life.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑基本上在你的一生中都在和自己对话。

sentences.en: And that's ongoing and, um, information from your body and information from the world merely
sentences.zh: 这种对话一直在进行，嗯，来自身体的信息和来自世界的信息只是

sentences.en: modulate that ongoing activity.
sentences.zh: 在调节这种正在进行的活动。

sentences.en: And that is the way the brain works.
sentences.zh: 这就是大脑的工作方式。

sentences.en: It's fine to say, and, and therapists know this, they use different words, but it's exactly
sentences.zh: 这样说是对的，治疗师们也知道这一点，他们用不同的词汇，但道理完全

sentences.en: the same idea that the brain is running a model of the world, an internal model of the world.
sentences.zh: 一样，即大脑在运行一个世界的模型，一个世界的内部模型。

sentences.en: That's not quite right.
sentences.zh: 这其实不太对。

sentences.en: The brain is a model and it's a model of the body as it receives information from the world.
sentences.zh: 大脑本身就是一个模型，它是当身体接收到来自世界的信息时，对身体建立的一个模型。

sentences.en: So we don't model the world.
sentences.zh: 所以我们并不是在模拟世界。

sentences.en: We model the information that arrives to our sensory surfaces, like our retinas and our cochlea and so on and so forth, and all the sensory surfaces inside our body.
sentences.zh: 我们在模拟到达我们感觉表面的信息，比如我们的视网膜、耳蜗等等，以及我们身体内部所有的感觉表面。

sentences.en: And the brain is receiving this information and it's attempting to make sense of it so that it knows what to do next to keep itself alive and well.
sentences.zh: 大脑接收这些信息并试图去理解它，这样它就知道接下来该做什么，以维持自身的生命和健康。

sentences.en: And it's using past experience to make these guesses.
sentences.zh: 它正在利用过去的经验来做出这些猜测。

sentences.en: So what you see and what you hear and what you smell and what you taste and so on, and what you feel in your body, because you don't really feel anything in your body.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的、听到的、闻到的、尝到的等等，以及你在身体里感觉到的——因为你其实并不是在身体里感觉任何东西。

sentences.en: You feel everything in your brain.
sentences.zh: 你是在大脑中感觉一切。

sentences.en: Everything is felt in your brain.
sentences.zh: 一切都是在大脑中被感受到的。

sentences.en: You see in your brain.
sentences.zh: 你在大脑中看。

sentences.en: You don't see in your eyes.
sentences.zh: 你不是在眼睛里看。

sentences.en: You hear in your brain.
sentences.zh: 你在大脑中听。

sentences.en: You don't hear it in your ears.
sentences.zh: 你不是在耳朵里听。

sentences.en: Um, everything you experience and everything you do is a combination of what's in the world, and in your body, because from your brain's perspective, that's the, that's outside the
sentences.zh: 嗯，你体验到的一切和你做的一切，都是世界上的东西与身体里的东西的结合，因为从你大脑的角度来看，那是，那是头骨

sentences.en: skull, right?
sentences.zh: 外部的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: So what's in the world, what's in the periphery and what's in the past that your brain re-implements as the present.
sentences.zh: 所以，存在于世界中的、存在于周边的、以及存在于过去并被你的大脑作为现在重新实现的东西。

sentences.en: Let's turn to your work on emotion, which is also fascinating.
sentences.zh: 让我们转向你关于情绪的工作，这也非常迷人。

sentences.en: And one of the big ideas that you've developed is that the emotions aren't things that happen to us, but there's something that our brain constructs.
sentences.zh: 你提出的一个核心观点是，情绪不是发生在我们身上的事情，而是我们的大脑构建出来的东西。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下这个。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是的。

sentences.en: In 25 words.
sentences.zh: 用25个字。

sentences.en: In 25, yeah, right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 用25个字，对，没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you, what goes along with this idea that we're born with these ancient circuits, right, deep, very deep inside our brain, kind of hardwired already there is this
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你，伴随着这种观点——即我们生来就带有这些古老的回路，对吧，深藏在我们大脑的最深处，某种程度上已经硬编码并在那里了——与之相伴的是

sentences.en: idea that emotions happen to you.
sentences.zh: 情绪发生在你身上的这种观点。

sentences.en: Something happens in the world, like you see a snake, and it triggers fear.
sentences.zh: 世界上发生了某事，比如你看到了一条蛇，它引发了恐惧。

sentences.en: And then fear produces this whole cascade of events.
sentences.zh: 然后恐惧引发了一连串的事件。

sentences.en: You make a particular facial expression, your heart rate goes up, maybe you freeze or you run.
sentences.zh: 你做出特定的面部表情，你的心率上升，也许你吓僵了或者逃跑了。

sentences.en: And the idea is that this, you know, that this is universal with everybody in the world.
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，你知道，这对于世界上每个人来说都是普遍的。

sentences.en: Everybody who has a neurotypical brain, who has these circuits, which, you know, are derived
sentences.zh: 每一个拥有神经典型大脑的人，拥有这些回路的人——这些回路，你知道，是

sentences.en: from ancient mammals or were, you know, evolved in hunter-gatherer society, you know, in Africa or whatever.
sentences.zh: 从古代哺乳动物演变而来的，或者是在猎人采集社会中，你知道的，在非洲或其他地方演变而来的。

sentences.en: There are different versions of it.
sentences.zh: 它有不同的版本。

sentences.en: And I'm painting kind of a, you know, you might want to say it's a straw man sort of a description, but, you know, you can add bells and whistles and nuances, but the basic idea
sentences.zh: 我在这里画了一幅，你知道，你可能会说这是一种稻草人式的描述，但是，你知道的，你可以加上各种修饰和细微差别，但基本观点

sentences.en: is that emotions are universal.
sentences.zh: 是情绪是普遍的。

sentences.en: They have a single set, you know, anger is, is, has a single set of features, maybe with some variation, but not so much variation that you can't recognize it in someone's face or
sentences.zh: 它们有一套单一的，你知道，愤怒是，拥有单一的一组特征，也许会有一些变异，但不会变异到你在别人的脸上

sentences.en: in their body or in their body movements or in their voice or whatever.
sentences.zh: 或在他们的身体里，或在他们的肢体动作中，或在他们的声音中认不出它的程度。

sentences.en: And all I can say is, I know it feels that way.
sentences.zh: 我所能说的是，我知道感觉确实如此。

sentences.en: It feels that way to me too.
sentences.zh: 对我来说也是这种感觉。

sentences.en: You know, when I get angry, when I'm, you know, when I feel gratitude or any rush of emotion
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我生气时，当我，你知道，当我感到感激或任何情绪涌上心头时，

sentences.en: to me feels exactly the same way as it feels to you, but that is not how the brain works.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，其感觉和你感受到的完全一样，但大脑并不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: And that is not what the evidence shows.
sentences.zh: 证据也不是这样显示的。

sentences.en: I mean, so the evidence shows really clearly, it couldn't be clearer, frankly, that emotions are not universal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，证据非常清楚地表明，坦率地说，不可能再清楚了，情绪并不是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: What is universal, however, is that the human brain is constantly constructing experience.
sentences.zh: 然而，普遍存在的是，人脑在不断地构建体验。

sentences.en: It's constantly trying to make sense of the world around and the body, or actually, I would
sentences.zh: 它不断地试图去理解周围的世界和身体，或者实际上，我会

sentences.en: say it's trying to make sense of what's going on inside the body in relation to what's going on around us inside, outside in the world.
sentences.zh: 说它试图去理解身体内部正在发生的事情，以及它与我们周围世界内外发生的事情的关系。

sentences.en: And it's doing this using past experience and it's always doing this.
sentences.zh: 它利用过去的经验来做到这一点，而且它一直在这样做。

sentences.en: So the way I would say it is kind of like this, the evidence to me suggests very strongly
sentences.zh: 所以我想表达的方式大约是这样的：在我看来，证据强烈地表明

sentences.en: that your brain receives sense data from the world, sights and sounds and smells and so on, and it receives sense data from the body.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑从世界接收感官数据，如视觉、声音、气味等，并且它接收来自身体的感官数据。

sentences.en: And so when there's a loud bang or a tug in your chest, your brain receives that information as the outcomes of some set of causes.
sentences.zh: 因此，当发生一声巨响或胸口一阵紧缩时，你的大脑将该信息作为某种原因组合的结果来接收。

sentences.en: But what caused that loud bang?
sentences.zh: 但是是什么引起了那声巨响？

sentences.en: Is it a car backfiring?
sentences.zh: 是汽车回火吗？

sentences.en: Is it somebody slamming a door?
sentences.zh: 是有人摔门吗？

sentences.en: Is it a gunshot?
sentences.zh: 是枪声吗？

sentences.en: What's happening?
sentences.zh: 发生什么事了？

sentences.en: You know, what caused that tug in your chest?
sentences.zh: 你知道，是什么引起了胸口的紧缩感？

sentences.en: Is it anxiety?
sentences.zh: 是焦虑吗？

sentences.en: Is it that you overate?
sentences.zh: 是你吃多了吗？

sentences.en: You know, too much.
sentences.zh: 你知道，吃得太多。

sentences.en: You have heartburn from like, you know, eating too rich of a meal.
sentences.zh: 你因为吃了过于油腻的饭菜而胃灼热。

sentences.en: Well, is it the beginning of a heart attack?
sentences.zh: 或者，这是心脏病发作的开始吗？

sentences.en: Your brain actually doesn't know.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑其实并不知道。

sentences.en: It only receives the outcomes.
sentences.zh: 它只能接收到结果。

sentences.en: It has to guess at what the causes are.
sentences.zh: 它必须猜测原因是什么。

sentences.en: This is called an inverse problem.
sentences.zh: 这被称为逆向问题。

sentences.en: You know what the outcome is.
sentences.zh: 你知道结果是什么。

sentences.en: You don't know what the cause is.
sentences.zh: 但你不知道原因是什么。

sentences.en: And so your brain has one other source of information available to it.
sentences.zh: 所以你的大脑可以利用另一个信息来源。

sentences.en: And that is past experience.
sentences.zh: 那就是过去的经验。

sentences.en: Memory.
sentences.zh: 记忆。

sentences.en: So it's not like you walk around consciously remembering things in order to perceive the world.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不意味着你四处走动时会有意识地记住事情来感知世界。

sentences.en: Your brain is constantly remembering, meaning it is constantly reassembling bits and pieces of past experience in order to make sense of what's going on in the body in relation to
sentences.zh: 你的大脑在不断地记忆，这意味着它不断地重新组合过去经验的零碎片段，以便理解身体内部与

sentences.en: the world so that your brain knows what to do next.
sentences.zh: 世界的关系，从而让大脑知道下一步该做什么。

sentences.en: Because frankly, if a loud bang is a door slamming, you would do something different in a particular situation than, you know, if it was a gunfire, if it was a gunshot.
sentences.zh: 因为坦率地说，如果一声巨响是关门声，在特定情况下你做出的反应会与如果是枪声时不同。

sentences.en: And so what your brain is, you know, if you were, if you were to, you know, anthropomorphize
sentences.zh: 所以你的大脑，如果你，如果你要，你知道，拟人化

sentences.en: a bit, you'd say, you know, what your brain is constantly doing is it's asking the question, what is similar in my past?
sentences.zh: 一点的话，你会说，你的大脑一直在做的是它在问这个问题：我过去有什么相似的经历？

sentences.en: What is similar to what this sensory array looks like and what caused it?
sentences.zh: 什么与这个感官阵列相似？是什么引起的？

sentences.en: And what did I do about it?
sentences.zh: 我当时是怎么处理的？

sentences.en: And did it work?
sentences.zh: 管用吗？

sentences.en: Now, in psychology, things that are similar to one another are a category.
sentences.zh: 在心理学中，彼此相似的事物构成了一个类别。

sentences.en: So your brain, you could say, is constructing categories.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，你的大脑正在构建类别。

sentences.en: It's a category construction organ.
sentences.zh: 它是一个类别构建器官。

sentences.en: It's constantly using the past to construct categories to make sense of the present in order for the purposes of guiding action and regulating metabolism.
sentences.zh: 它不断地利用过去来构建类别，以理解当下，从而达到指导行动和调节新陈代谢的目的。

sentences.en: But we also know that a representation of a category is a concept.
sentences.zh: 但我们也知道，对类别的表征就是一个概念。

sentences.en: So you could say also that what the brain is doing is it's doing concept generation, ad hoc concept generation.
sentences.zh: 所以你也可以说，大脑在做的是概念生成，即兴概念生成。

sentences.en: Your brain is constantly remembering, reassembling past experience as concepts that are tailored
sentences.zh: 你的大脑在不断地记忆，将过去的经验重新组合成量身定制的概念

sentences.en: to the specific situation that you're in to make sense of what your body means in that particular situation so that it knows what to do next to keep you alive and well.
sentences.zh: 以适应你所处的具体情境，去理解你的身体在那种特定情境下的意义，这样它就知道接下来该做什么来维持你的生命和健康。

sentences.en: And that's what emotions are.
sentences.zh: 这就是情绪。

sentences.en: Emotions are just when your brain uses past experiences of emotion to make meaning of the present and guide action.
sentences.zh: 情绪不过是大脑利用过去的情绪经验来赋予当下意义并指导行动的时候。

sentences.en: If emotion is something that our brain creates, then can we will ourselves to feel emotions differently?
sentences.zh: 如果情绪是我们大脑创造的，那么我们能否用意志力让自己的情绪感受有所不同？

sentences.en: I mean, how much control do we actually have over our emotions?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们对自己的情绪到底有多少控制力？

sentences.en: Well, I would say that we definitely can, but it's much harder to do than actually sometimes we make it out to be.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会说我们绝对可以，但这比我们有时想象的要难得多。

sentences.en: And every client that every therapist has ever had knows this to be true.
sentences.zh: 每个治疗师接待过的每个来访者都知道这是真的。

sentences.en: It's actually very, very hard to do.
sentences.zh: 这其实非常非常难做到。

sentences.en: And also what it means is that what control looks like doesn't only happen in the moment when a person wants to change how they feel.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着，所谓的控制并不只发生在一个人想要改变自己感受的那一瞬间。

sentences.en: So one thing I haven't done is made the distinction between affect and emotion, and that's a really important distinction in the science that we do.
sentences.zh: 所以有一件事我还没做，那就是区分效价（affect）与情绪，在我们开展的科学研究中，这是一个非常重要的区分。

sentences.en: You know, emotions are easier to change.
sentences.zh: 你知道，情绪更容易改变。

sentences.en: Affect is not as easy to change in the moment.
sentences.zh: 而效价在当下没那么容易改变。

sentences.en: So let me back up a little bit and explain that distinction, and then I will answer your question.
sentences.zh: 所以我退回一点，解释一下这种区别，然后我来回答你的问题。

sentences.en: Your brain is always controlling your body, and your body is always sending sense data back to your brain.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑一直在控制你的身体，而你的身体也一直在向大脑发送感官数据。

sentences.en: And for the most part, we are not aware of all of those sense data to the same degree that we're aware of sights and sounds and smells and things.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，我们并没有意识到所有这些感官数据，其程度不如我们意识到视觉、听觉、嗅觉等事物那样明显。

sentences.en: At least I hope you're not.
sentences.zh: 至少我希望你没有意识到。

sentences.en: If you are aware of what's going on inside your body, I feel really bad for you because it means that you've got a whole drama unfolding there.
sentences.zh: 如果你意识到身体内部正在发生什么，我真为你感到难过，因为这意味着那里正在上演一整出戏。

sentences.en: And if you're aware of it, that means that you're probably in significant discomfort, and
sentences.zh: 如果你意识到了，那就意味着你可能正处于极大的痛苦中，

sentences.en: I'm really sorry.
sentences.zh: 我深表遗憾。

sentences.en: Um, but what evolution has done is made available that information to us as affect, as simple feelings.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是进化所做的是将这些信息作为效价（affect）、作为简单的感觉提供给我们。

sentences.en: I feel pleasant.
sentences.zh: 我觉得愉快。

sentences.en: I feel unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 我觉得不愉快。

sentences.en: I feel worked up.
sentences.zh: 我觉得情绪激动。

sentences.en: I feel calm.
sentences.zh: 我觉得平静。

sentences.en: I feel comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得舒适。

sentences.en: I feel uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得不舒服。

sentences.en: So your brain is regulating your body 24-7.
sentences.zh: 所以你的大脑全天候24/7地在调节你的身体。

sentences.en: Your body is sending information back to your brain 24-7, and you feel affect 24-7, regardless of whether you're emotional or not.
sentences.zh: 你的身体全天候24/7地向大脑发回信息，而你无论是否有情绪，也全天候24/7地感受到效价。

sentences.en: You feel affect.
sentences.zh: 你能感受到效价。

sentences.en: Affect is universal.
sentences.zh: 效价是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: Now, what affective features are associated with different things is not necessarily universal always, but affect is universal.
sentences.zh: 现在，与不同事物相关联的效价特征不一定总是普遍的，但效价本身是普遍的。

sentences.en: The ability that the capacity to have affect is universal, and most likely all mammals and
sentences.zh: 拥有效价的能力是普遍存在的，极有可能所有的哺乳动物和

sentences.en: many vertebrates, probably maybe all vertebrates, and maybe even some invertebrates can also feel affect.
sentences.zh: 许多脊椎动物，可能甚至所有的脊椎动物，甚至某些无脊椎动物也能感受到效价。

sentences.en: That's a, you know, that's an interesting, you know, morass of confusion there, but it's interesting to talk about and think about.
sentences.zh: 这是一个，你知道的，一个有趣的混乱泥潭，但谈论和思考它很有意思。

sentences.en: But, you know, I would say affect is definitely not a human-specific ability.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我会说效价绝对不是人类特有的能力。

sentences.en: And sometimes when we're making meaning of the sensations and the affect that goes with it, sometimes we make episodes of emotion by, again,
sentences.zh: 有时，当我们赋予身体的感受以及与之相伴的效价以意义时，有时我们会通过再次

sentences.en: creating categories or concepts on the fly.
sentences.zh: 在飞行中（即即兴）创建类别或概念来制造情绪片段。

sentences.en: In fact, there's a convenient term called a conceptual category, which means that the concept that knowledge
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一个方便的术语叫做概念类别，这意味着概念即知识

sentences.en: is what makes a bunch of things similar to each other in a category, because a bunch of things can be similar to each other by virtue of their function,
sentences.zh: 正是它使得类别中的一堆事物彼此相似，因为一堆事物可以通过它们的功能彼此相似，

sentences.en: not by virtue of what they look like or smell like or sound like or taste like.
sentences.zh: 而不是通过它们的外表、气味、声音或味道彼此相似。

sentences.en: And many things that we deal with in life are categories of that sort, and infants learn those kinds of categories in the first year of infancy.
sentences.zh: 我们在生活中处理的许多事情都是这类类别，婴儿在婴儿期的第一年就学会了这些类别的存在。

sentences.en: They're called abstract categories, where what the similarity that draws the instances together are not perceptual.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为抽象类别，其中将实例汇集在一起的相似性不是感知上的。

sentences.en: They are functional.
sentences.zh: 它们是功能性的。

sentences.en: That is, they serve some kind of function.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它们具有某种功能。

sentences.en: And this is something I talk about in Seven and a Half Lessons.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在《七堂半脑科学课》中讨论过的内容。

sentences.en: And so, affect is hard to change, because you don't have volitional control over your heart and your lungs.
sentences.zh: 因此，效价很难改变，因为你无法对你的心脏和肺进行意志控制。

sentences.en: You do have volitional control over your breathing, and you can try to practice breathing in order to calm your heart and, you know, control your heart and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 你的确对自己的呼吸有自主控制权，你可以尝试练习呼吸来平静心脏，你知道的，控制心脏等等。

sentences.en: But you can't stop your blood from flowing.
sentences.zh: 但你无法阻止血液流动。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: And so, and you can't, it's really, most people can't speed their heart up just by thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你不能，这真的，大多数人无法仅靠思考来加速心跳。

sentences.en: And, you know, so affect is actually really hard to change without drugs, like in the instant, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，情绪实际上真的很难在不借助药物的情况下改变，比如在瞬间，你知道的。

sentences.en: And that's really often why people use drugs, both prescription, you know, chemicals and unprescribed chemicals, because they're attempting to relieve discomfort or distress,
sentences.zh: 这往往就是人们使用药物的原因，无论是处方药，你知道的，化学物质，还是非处方化学物质，因为他们试图缓解不适或痛苦，

sentences.en: which is affective in nature.
sentences.zh: 这些痛苦本质上就是情绪上的。

sentences.en: But you definitely can change how you make sense of affect and the sensations that give rise to it.
sentences.zh: 但你绝对可以改变你如何理解情绪以及产生情绪的感觉。

sentences.en: And, but there, I would say, in the moment, for example, what, what James Gross and others call, you know, reappraisal is just,
sentences.zh: 而且，但在这里，我想说，在当时，例如，詹姆斯·格罗斯和其他人所说的，你知道的，重新评价只是，

sentences.en: you could think of it mechanistically as your brain is recategorizing a set of, the set of sensations is recategorizing what they mean.
sentences.zh: 从机制上讲，你可以认为你的大脑正在重新分类一组感觉，这组感觉正在重新分类它们的含义。

sentences.en: That is, it's conjuring a different category, a different concept to make sense of those sensations and therefore give rise to a different action.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它在召唤一个不同的类别，一个不同的概念来理解这些感觉，从而产生不同的行动。

sentences.en: So, in the moment, you can do that very deliberately, but sometimes even that is really, really, really hard to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，在当时，你可以非常刻意地做到这一点，但有时候即使做到这一点也真的、真的很难。

sentences.en: So, and a one way to have more control over your emotions, in addition to just, you know, keeping, making it easier for your brain to regulate your body,
sentences.zh: 所以，除了你知道的，保持、让你的大脑更容易调节你的身体之外，掌控你的情绪的另一种方法是，

sentences.en: which is like get enough sleep, eat healthfully, you know, surround yourself with people who, you know, care about you and who you love and have good relationships with.
sentences.zh: 就像获得充足的睡眠、健康饮食、你知道的，周围都是你知道的、关心你、你爱的人并与他们保持良好关系的人。

sentences.en: In addition to those things, you know, you know, you can learn and practice reconceptualizing that is changing the categories that your brain can make easily.
sentences.zh: 除了这些事情，你知道，你知道，你可以学习和练习重新概念化，也就是改变你的大脑可以轻易产生的类别。

sentences.en: So, it's kind of like exercise, you know, or like driving, you know, first of all, it is like exercise because it's very effortful to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点像运动，你知道的，或者像开车，你知道的，首先，它就像运动，因为做这件事需要付出很大的努力。

sentences.en: And so, it's like an investment in a healthier you, but it is also like driving where at first it's really hard, but then when you practice it really a lot, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像是对更健康的你的一笔投资，但它也像开车，起初真的很难，但当你经常练习时，你知道的，

sentences.en: it gets easier and pretty automatic.
sentences.zh: 它会变得更容易，而且相当自动化。

sentences.en: So, you can take anxiety and turn it into determination or exhilaration even.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以把焦虑转化为决心，甚至是兴奋。

sentences.en: You can take anger and turn it into awe.
sentences.zh: 你可以把愤怒转化为敬畏。

sentences.en: The aspect stays the same, but the meaning is what's changing.
sentences.zh: 方面保持不变，但改变的是意义。

sentences.en: And if you practice in advance, you're like seeding your brain to be able to do this much more automatically.
sentences.zh: 如果你提前练习，你就像是在为你的大脑播种，使其能够更自动地做到这一点。

sentences.en: So, for example, you know, I'm like skeptical by nature,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，你知道，我天生比较怀疑，

sentences.en: but there is research to show that gratitude and compassion and awe are very good for your nervous system and therefore for your mental health.
sentences.zh: 但研究表明，感恩、同情和敬畏对你的神经系统非常好，因此对你的心理健康也非常好。

sentences.en: And right down the hall for me is a colleague who studies gratitude and the importance of gratitude.
sentences.zh: 就在我办公室走廊对面，有一位同事研究感恩以及感恩的重要性。

sentences.en: So, I'm like, okay, fine, you know, all right, I'll try it.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，好吧，好吧，你知道，好吧，我试试。

sentences.en: And so, I set myself the task of, you know, gratitude I was already on board with, but awe was a trickier one.
sentences.zh: 因此，我给自己设定了这样一个任务，你知道的，感恩我已经接受了，但敬畏是一个更棘手的问题。

sentences.en: So, I thought, all right, I'll try to, you know, cultivate a sense of wonder for five minutes every day where, you know, I'm a SPAC and therefore my problems are a SPAC and,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，好吧，我会试着，你知道的，每天花五分钟培养一种惊叹感，在那里，你知道的，我是一个太空人，因此我的问题是太空问题，并且，

sentences.en: you know, let's see if I can do it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，看看我能不能做到。

sentences.en: And sure enough, you know, it was hard at first, but I did it just like, you know, I learned to, you know, do a plank, hold a plank for a minute or two, whatever.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，你知道的，起初很难，但我做到了，就像，你知道的，我学会了，你知道的，做一个平板支撑，坚持一分钟或两分钟，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And, um, and eventually it became really easy.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，最终它变得非常容易。

sentences.en: And now I can switch in and out of, you know, that particular, um, state, my brain can make it easily when I need it.
sentences.zh: 现在我可以自由切换进出，你知道的，那种特定的，嗯，状态，当我需要时，我的大脑可以轻易地创造它。

sentences.en: And, um, and give my nervous system, you know, if you're a SPAC for a minute, your, your problems are a SPAC for a minute, and that gives you a break for a minute.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，给你的神经系统，你知道的，如果你当一分钟的太空人，你的，你的问题当一分钟的太空问题，这会给你一分钟的休息时间。

sentences.en: And that changes how you breathe and it changes how you comport your body and it changes what you do next.
sentences.zh: 这会改变你的呼吸方式，改变你的身体姿态，并改变你接下来要做的事情。

sentences.en: Um, so a lot of the things that we kind of know by different names, we misunderstand mechanistic way in which they occur, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们用不同名称了解的很多事情，我们误解了它们发生的机械方式，对吧？

sentences.en: So appraisal or reappraisal is a description of something that happens.
sentences.zh: 所以评价或重新评价是对发生的事情的描述。

sentences.en: It's not an explanation of the process that produces it.
sentences.zh: 它并不是对产生该过程的解释。

sentences.en: And by understanding how your brain works, you can generalize that process and start using it in new other ways.
sentences.zh: 通过了解你的大脑是如何工作的，你可以将该过程推广并开始以其他新的方式使用它。

sentences.en: So for example, you can learn other emotion concepts from other cultures that don't exist in our culture,
sentences.zh: 例如，你可以从其他文化中学习我们文化中不存在的其他情绪概念，

sentences.en: but that might be really useful for helping you to make sense of your affect and the sensations that give rise to it.
sentences.zh: 但这可能对帮助你理解你的情绪以及产生情绪的感觉非常有用。

sentences.en: So that you can broaden the repertoire of actions that you can potentially take.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以拓宽你潜在可以采取的行动方案。

sentences.en: And we know from the wonderful work of George Bonanno, that flexibility is the key to resilience in any situation, even a really stressful one.
sentences.zh: 我们从乔治·博纳诺的出色工作中得知，在任何情况下，甚至是压力极大的情况下，灵活性是适应力的关键。

sentences.en: And so that's a way you can control your emotional life, cultivate, cultivate your emotional life, architect your life,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你可以控制你的情感生活、培养、培养你的情感生活、构建你的生活的方式，

sentences.en: architect your experience in a way that is before the heat of the moment.
sentences.zh: 在情绪激动的时刻到来之前构建你的体验。

sentences.en: So what are the big unanswered questions in your field and what are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 那么，你所在领域中尚未解答的重大问题是什么？你现在正在研究什么？

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Well, I have a lab of 25 full-time people and, you know, a hundred or so undergraduate researchers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有一个由 25 名全职人员组成的实验室，还有大约一百名本科生研究人员。

sentences.en: So we have many, many questions that we are trying to understand.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有很多很多问题正在试图理解。

sentences.en: But one thing we're trying to understand, for example, is the name for your brain sensing your body is called interoception.
sentences.zh: 但我们试图理解的一件事，例如，你的大脑感知身体的名称被称为内感受。

sentences.en: And usually interoception is studied as your awareness of your physical sensation.
sentences.zh: 通常，内感受被研究为你对身体感觉的意识。

sentences.en: Are you aware of your heartbeat?
sentences.zh: 你意识到自己的心跳了吗？

sentences.en: Are you aware?
sentences.zh: 你意识到了吗？

sentences.en: But that's really a very small part of what interoception is.
sentences.zh: 但这其实只是内感受很小的一部分。

sentences.en: Your brain is estimating the state of your body.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑正在评估你身体的状态。

sentences.en: It's modeling your body, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它在模拟你的身体。

sentences.en: And most of that state estimation is happening outside of your awareness at all, completely.
sentences.zh: 而且大部分状态评估完全发生在你的意识之外。

sentences.en: You just have no awareness of it.
sentences.zh: 你根本没有意识到它。

sentences.en: And so that's a question we're really interested in.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们非常感兴趣的一个问题。

sentences.en: Not the question of, like, are you aware of your heartbeats?
sentences.zh: 不是诸如“你是否意识到自己的心跳”之类的问题。

sentences.en: But how well is your brain actually tracking what's happening in your body?
sentences.zh: 而是你的大脑实际上对身体发生的事情追踪得有多好？

sentences.en: Because one cause of depression, for example, could be that your brain has a mistaken model of your body.
sentences.zh: 因为抑郁症的一个原因，例如，可能是你的大脑对你的身体有一个错误的模型。

sentences.en: And there's some disconnect there.
sentences.zh: 其中存在某种脱节。

sentences.en: So that's one thing that we're really mechanistically trying to work out.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们正在从机制上努力解决的一件事。

sentences.en: Another is, you know, in the way that we understand some things, that we think something first and then we act.
sentences.zh: 另一个是，你知道的，在我们理解某些事情的方式中，我们先思考然后行动。

sentences.en: Or we think something first and then we feel something.
sentences.zh: 或者我们先思考然后感受某些事情。

sentences.en: So we go in and we try to tinker with how people think in order to change how they feel and what they do.
sentences.zh: 所以我们介入并试图篡改人们的思考方式，以改变他们的感受和行动。

sentences.en: But actually, the way the brain works is that your brain prepares your actions first and your experiences derive from that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，大脑的工作方式是，你的大脑首先准备你的行动，而你的体验由此产生。

sentences.en: It's not the other way around.
sentences.zh: 情况并非相反。

sentences.en: And this is also something that I explain in both books, actually.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在两本书中都解释过的事情。

sentences.en: And there's a very strong likelihood that what's happening is not that you think bad things and then you feel bad.
sentences.zh: 而且很有可能发生的情况不是你想到坏事然后你感觉不好。

sentences.en: More like you feel bad and that leads your brain to think bad things.
sentences.zh: 更像是你感觉不好，这导致你的大脑去想坏事。

sentences.en: So it could be that there are problems with the way that your brain is modeling your body or literally problems with your body.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是因为你的大脑模拟身体的方式有问题，或者字面意义上你的身体有问题。

sentences.en: For example, maybe your mitochondria are not as effective as they need to be.
sentences.zh: 例如，也许你的线粒体没有达到应有的效率。

sentences.en: And that could be a source of depression.
sentences.zh: 这可能是抑郁症的根源。

sentences.en: That could be a source of, you know, this disconnect.
sentences.zh: 这可能是你知道的这种脱节的根源。

sentences.en: Your brain is attempting to model your body.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑正试图模拟你的身体。

sentences.en: Your body's not functioning well in this really, you know, subtle way that you would not be aware of.
sentences.zh: 你的身体在这个你不会意识到的微妙方面并没有很好地运作。

sentences.en: But maybe you'd just be aware of feeling bad and that that is actually what's driving those negative thoughts, not the other way around.
sentences.zh: 但也许你只会意识到感觉不好，而这实际上才是驱动那些负面想法的原因，而不是相反。

sentences.en: To me, this seems, first of all, very plausible from a neuroscience standpoint.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，首先，从神经科学的角度来看，这似乎非常合理。

sentences.en: And what it means is that when we go in and we get people to change how they think in order to change how they feel, what we're doing is actually just breaking a cycle.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，当我们介入并让人们改变他们的思考方式以改变他们的感受时，我们实际上只是在打破一个循环。

sentences.en: We're not changing the cause of the problem.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有改变问题的根源。

sentences.en: We're just interrupting an ongoing cycle.
sentences.zh: 我们只是中断了一个正在进行的循环。

sentences.en: And, again, I would say there are real lessons there about things that you might want to do differently if this is actually – it's not that what we're doing is bad.
sentences.zh: 而且，再次我想说，如果这确实是——并不是说我们正在做的事情不好，这里面确实有一些值得借鉴的教训，告诉你可能想要做一些不同的事情。

sentences.en: It's just that there might be additional things that we might want to think about doing for treating mental illness.
sentences.zh: 只是我们在治疗精神疾病时可能还想考虑做一些额外的事情。

sentences.en: Well, it just sounds amazing, the work that you're doing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你正在做的工作听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: I really appreciate you taking the time to speak with me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天花时间和我交谈。

sentences.en: And I highly recommend – I mean, maybe I shouldn't say this, but I think your new book is very accessible and a great read.
sentences.zh: 我强烈推荐——我的意思是，也许我不该这么说，但我认为你的新书非常平易近人，是一本非常棒的读物。

sentences.en: So, I appreciate the time that you've taken.
sentences.zh: 所以，我很感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。
